newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Nicaragua president to visit Taiwan from Aug 5.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua president to visit Taiwan from Aug 5.

text.p: Nicaraguan President Arnoldo Aleman plans to arrive in Taiwan on August 5 for a five-day trip, the foreign ministry said on Saturday.
Nicaragua is one of only 30 countries that recognise Taipei rather than its arch-rival Beijing.

Aleman, whose government recently signed a letter supporting U.N. membership for Taiwan's exiled government, will meet with Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui during his visit to the island, the ministry said.
"(President Aleman) also will meet with various leaders of our government and industries," Taipei's foreign ministry said in a statement.
On Tuesday Nicaraguan U.N. ambassador Enrique Paguaga Fernandez denounced threats by China against his country's support for Taiwan's membership of the world body.
Beijing took over China's U.N. seat in 1971 when Taiwan, to which the Nationalist Chinese government retreated in 1949 following a civil war, was expelled from the United Nations.
China regards the island as a renegade province and reacts fiercely to any move to recognise or seat Taiwan.
In July Nicaragua and eight other allies of Taiwan signed a letter asking the General Assembly to discuss granting Taiwan U.N. membership during its opening session in September.
China has prevented similar proposals from winning inscription on the U.N. agenda for four consecutive years.
